solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Invest in Napoleonic rifle given tip from enthusiast

parts.note: Napoleon spoke French, and the French for 'in' is en
to rifle a drawer is to rob it

indicators.note: the tip of a word is its first letter, taken here from the following word

explanation.surface: Someone puts money into an old French firearm on the advice of a keen collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invest' looks financial, but it is the old sense of clothing someone in robes of office.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words mean to clothe ceremonially, investing a bishop by dressing him in his robes.

clue.text: Commission unit in printing trade to check circular letter

parts.note: an em is a printer's unit of measure, the width of a letter M

indicators.note: to check something is to hold it in, so one piece holds the other

parts.note: to ply a trade is to work at it, so ply can stand for trade
O is the letter shaped like a circle

explanation.surface: A print-trade union branch is commissioned to vet a circular sent to members.
explanation.definitionFit: To commission someone is to engage them for work, which is a synonym of hiring them.

clue.text: Ceremony heard opposite to home yesterday

indicators.note: heard tells us the word for ceremony is to be taken by its sound, not its spelling

parts.note: a rite is a ceremony
a football team plays either at home or away

explanation.surface: A ritual that sounds like the reverse of yesterday's home fixture.
explanation.walkthrough: 'yesterday' is the impatient boss's 'I want it yesterday', meaning at once.
explanation.definitionFit: Demanding something yesterday is an idiom for wanting it immediately, without any delay.

clue.text: Footwear in stock going to the Spanish plant

parts.note: stock is a broth made from bones or vegetables
el is Spanish for 'the'
a creeper is a plant such as ivy that spreads along surfaces

explanation.surface: Boots kept in stock are shipped to a Spanish factory.
explanation.walkthrough: BROTHEL CREEPERS are thick crepe-soled suede shoes, worn by British Teddy Boys in the 1950s.
explanation.definitionFit: These suede shoes with thick crepe soles are a particular style of footwear.

clue.text: Kinky desires involving newspaper's centre spread

indicators.note: involving means taking in, so the shuffled letters wrap round another
kinky means twisted, so the letters of desires are bent into a new order
the centre of a word is its middle letter, here of newspaper

explanation.surface: Racy fantasies fill a tabloid's middle pages.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kinky' shuffles DESIRES into DISERSE, which takes in P, the middle letter of 'newspaper's'. 'centre spread' tempts as one phrase, but 'spread' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: To disperse things is to scatter them widely, which is to spread them out.

clue.text: Welshman and an American avoiding canteen that's erected

indicators.note: erected means set upright, so in a down answer the letters read from the bottom up
avoiding means leaving out, so a letter is dropped from the canteen

parts.note: the NAAFI runs canteens for British forces
A can stand for American

explanation.surface: A Welshman and an American skip the army canteen, which stands tall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'avoiding' drops one A from NAAFI to give NAFI, which 'that's erected' turns upside down.
explanation.definitionFit: Ifan is the Welsh form of the name John, so it fits a man from Wales.

clue.text: Period at night when newsman tucks into shellfish

indicators.note: to tuck into is to go inside, as well as to eat heartily

parts.note: a prawn is a shellfish
ED is short for editor, a newspaper man

explanation.surface: The point in the evening when a journalist digs into a seafood dinner.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tucks into' suggests eating, but here it signals one piece going inside the other.
explanation.definitionFit: The dark hours just before sunrise are still technically night-time.

clue.text: Approach game having subdued Athenian character with power

indicators.note: subdued puts one thing under another, so in this down answer the game sits on top of the letter

parts.note: RU is rugby union
nu is a letter of the Greek alphabet
P is the physics symbol for power

explanation.surface: A sporting contest where the Greek side has been beaten into submission by force.
explanation.definitionFit: The run-up to an event is the period of approach leading to it.

clue.text: 21 maybe did this dessert during previous day

indicators.note: during means within, so the dessert sits inside the other pieces

parts.note: ex means former or previous, as in an ex-partner
a torte is a rich cake served as a dessert

explanation.surface: A swindler cooked up a pudding the day before.
explanation.walkthrough: 21 is CONMAN; a con man might well have extracted money by threats.
explanation.definitionFit: Extorting money by force or threats is a typical activity of a swindler.

clue.text: One fancied Aguero to score regularly during leg

indicators.note: during means within, so the picked letters go inside

parts.note: pins is slang for legs

indicators.note: regularly means taking every other letter, here the even ones

explanation.surface: The Argentine striker Sergio Aguero is expected to score in each leg of a tie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One fancied' is a bird kept by a pigeon fancier, not a fancied football team.
explanation.definitionFit: Pigeon fanciers breed and race these birds, so a pigeon is one that is fancied.

clue.text: Girl's teachers that can be found in bar

definitions.text: that can be found in bar

parts.note: Hazel is a girl's name
the NUT was the National Union of Teachers

explanation.surface: A girl's teachers might be spotted drinking in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'bar' suggests a pub, but it is a bar of chocolate.
explanation.definitionFit: Chocolate bars often contain pieces of this nut, as in fruit and nut bars.

clue.text: See 3
Eccentric abroad joins the spiritual course

indicators.note: joins says one piece is placed next to the next

parts.note: out can mean away from home, as abroad does
RE is religious education, a school subject

explanation.surface: An oddball overseas signs up for a religious studies class.
explanation.definitionFit: Ideas described as far-out or weird are colloquially said to be way off in space, i.e. eccentric.

clue.text: Gemstone's origin found in jeweller's, typically

indicators.note: the origin of a word is its first letter

parts.note: as per means as usual, typically

explanation.surface: Where a gem comes from can usually be traced in the jeweller's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an opaque variety of quartz, usually red, used as a semi-precious stone.

clue.text: Governor over prison, Bren perhaps, welcoming one that's given bird

indicators.note: over puts the first piece above the next in a down answer

parts.note: an emperor governs an empire
pen is slang for a prison, short for penitentiary

indicators.note: welcoming means taking in, so the gun holds the digit-like letter

parts.note: the Bren is a type of light machine gun
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A prison governor greets an inmate who has been sentenced.
explanation.walkthrough: 'given bird' looks like prison slang (bird = time inside), but 'bird' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the largest species of Antarctic penguin, a flightless seabird.

clue.text: US politician idiotic to well-read man

indicators.note: idiotic means senseless, so the letters lose their sensible order

explanation.surface: An American politician is called a fool by a bookish man.
explanation.definitionFit: He was a Democrat senator, vice-president under Carter and 1984 presidential candidate.

clue.text: Sally ventilates three-wheeler

parts.note: airs means ventilates, as when airing a room
a trike is a tricycle

explanation.surface: A woman called Sally opens up her tricycle to let air in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sally' looks like a name but is a military sortie.
explanation.definitionFit: A sally is a sudden attack, and bombing from aircraft is one such attack.

clue.text: Buster catches ball finally after second game

indicators.note: after puts the second piece following the first
catches means holds, so the actor's name takes in a letter

parts.note: Buster Crabbe was an Olympic swimmer and film actor who played Flash Gordon

indicators.note: finally picks the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A fielder holds the ball at the end of the second match.
explanation.definitionFit: Scrabble is a board game of making words from letter tiles.

clue.text: Desire Geordie life in bit of mischief and spice

indicators.note: in places the run of pieces inside the prank

parts.note: a caper is a prank, a bit of mischief
a yen is a longing or desire
a Geordie comes from Newcastle, in the North East (NE) of England
pep means energy, life

explanation.surface: A Newcastle native wants a lively prank that adds spice to life.
explanation.definitionFit: This hot powdered chilli is a common kitchen seasoning.

clue.text: Retired academic retaining a cherished computer

indicators.note: retired means gone back, so the whole is read in reverse, upwards in this down answer
retaining means holding on to, so the teacher holds the other pieces

parts.note: a don is a university teacher
pet means favourite, cherished

explanation.surface: An elderly lecturer keeps hold of a beloved old computer.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer 'Retired' means the whole assembly reads upwards, after 'retaining' has the academic hold the other two pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: A small portable computer was once marketed as a notepad PC.

clue.text: See 14
He deceptively takes business partner to a curry without money

parts.note: CO is short for company, a business

indicators.note: without means outside, so the bread surrounds the letter

parts.note: nan bread is served with a curry

explanation.surface: A man takes his business partner for a curry and leaves him to pay.
explanation.definitionFit: A swindler is someone who cheats people out of money by trickery.

clue.text: Friar is told to trim borders for toff

indicators.note: trimming the borders cuts letters from both ends of the phrase, leaving its inside

explanation.surface: A friar is instructed to cut the edges of something, perhaps a hedge or his tonsure.
explanation.definitionFit: A toff is an upper-class person, an aristocrat in casual British slang.

clue.text: Language militants used on TV panel show

parts.note: the IRA is the Irish Republican Army
QI is a British quiz show hosted by Stephen Fry and later Sandi Toksvig

explanation.surface: Bad words from terrorists are aired on a television quiz.
explanation.definitionFit: The Arabic dialect spoken in Baghdad and elsewhere in that country is a form of speech.

clue.text: It's blown over after company Romeo clear of all charges

indicators.note: after places the first piece following the others

parts.note: Romeo is R in the radio alphabet
a nett sum has had all deductions taken off
O is the cricket abbreviation for over

explanation.surface: A Romeo is cleared of charges once the company's case is over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's blown' is not a fuse but a wind instrument; a Cornetto is also a British ice-cream cone.
explanation.definitionFit: This is an old wooden wind instrument with finger holes and a cup mouthpiece, played by blowing.

clue.text: Expert crosses Montana's number one peak

indicators.note: crosses here means goes across, so one piece spans the other

parts.note: an ace is an expert

indicators.note: number one means the first letter of the word

explanation.surface: A seasoned climber traverses the highest summit in Montana.
explanation.definitionFit: The acme is the highest point of something, its summit.

clue.text: Acting group sing quietly in support

indicators.note: in says the first two pieces go inside the support

parts.note: to back is to support
to sing to the police, or rat, is to inform
P is piano, quietly in music

explanation.surface: Singers perform softly as backing vocals.
explanation.walkthrough: The Brat Pack were young Hollywood actors of the 1980s.
explanation.definitionFit: The name was given to a group of young film actors who often appeared together.

clue.text: School full of quadrangles?

parts.note: a school of art whose paintings were full of geometric shapes, posing as a college with many quads

explanation.surface: A school or college with lots of courtyards.
explanation.walkthrough: Quadrangles are college courtyards, but here they are four-sided figures, and the school is an art movement.
explanation.definitionFit: This early twentieth-century art movement of Picasso and Braque broke subjects into geometric shapes.

clue.text: One ultimately extra wicked controlling swindle?

definitions.text: One ultimately extra wicked controlling swindle?

indicators.note: ultimately picks the last letter of the word
controlling means holding in, so the comparative holds the cheat

parts.note: viler means more wicked
to do someone is to swindle them

explanation.surface: Someone even more wicked in charge of a con.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoer, especially one who is very wicked, as a swindle-running criminal is.

clue.text: Trainee during academic period preferring noon finish

parts.note: in means during, as in 'in the night'

indicators.note: preferring noon as a finish swaps the last letter for N, the abbreviation for noon

parts.note: a term is a period of the academic year

explanation.surface: A student during the school term would rather leave at midday.
explanation.definitionFit: An apprentice or junior doctor learning on the job is a trainee.
